purpose: Synthetic traversal evidence for tenant-to-auth-event context. Covers bounded tenant event context, delegated or shared-service weak context, similar-label near miss, stale historical event suppression, provider or health-check suppression, and high-cardinality fan-out. All identifiers, sources, and timestamps are synthetic.

allowed_assertions: A bounded synthetic tenant-to-auth-event edge can be presented as tenant-scoped auth-event context.
blocked_assertions: Do not infer tenant ownership, compromise, actor control, maliciousness, operational effect, direct user intent, current access, or final assessment from a tenant-event edge alone.
Tenant-event context is a scoped observation, not an identity validation or trust-boundary conclusion.

allowed_assertions: A delegated or shared-service synthetic event can be retained as weak access-path context that still needs corroboration.
blocked_assertions: Do not promote a delegated or shared-service event to tenant ownership, compromise, direct user action, actor control, current access, or final assessment without corroboration from tenant-scoped administrative evidence and role context.
Do not treat shared-service context as a normal user traversal.

allowed_assertions: A similarly named synthetic auth event connected to another synthetic tenant can co-exist in the graph without being tenant-scoped evidence for this source tenant.
blocked_assertions: Do not join the source tenant to auth-event nodes based on similar labels, naming conventions, or shared fixture prefixes.
Do not infer tenant ownership, compromise, actor control, direct user intent, or final assessment from label overlap.

suppressed_targets.reason: Recorded auth event is historical only (firstseen 2018-02-10, lastseen 2018-02-10) and outside the pattern's 30-day temporal window; the stale marker remains to make behavior visible even if temporal handling differs across implementations. It must not be presented as current access, active authentication context, compromise, or actor control.

allowed_assertions: The historical edge can remain available for audit, lifecycle analysis, or stale-context review if the downstream system keeps an explicit historical or suppression-bypass mode.
blocked_assertions: Stale or historical auth-event context is not current access, active session context, compromise, actor control, direct user intent, or final assessment.
Do not infer tenant ownership or operational effect from a stale auth event.

suppressed_targets.reason: Source tenant is listed in the multi_tenant_provider_or_demo_tenants negative-node list and target event is listed as synthetic_or_healthcheck_auth_events; ordinary output should suppress this service context.
Same suppression: provider/demo tenant and health-check event context can exist as audit evidence but should not be shown as a normal tenant access path.
Same suppression: provider/demo tenant fan-out is service or health-check context, not a normal user traversal.
Same suppression: provider/demo tenant fan-out exceeds the ordinary traversal intent and should remain suppression evidence.

allowed_assertions: The provider/demo and health-check evidence can remain available for audit, rarity calculation, or local suppression tuning.
blocked_assertions: Do not present provider, demo, service, automation, or health-check context as a normal user traversal.
Do not infer tenant ownership, compromise, actor control, direct user intent, operational effect, or final assessment from provider/demo health-check edges.

allowed_assertions: The high-cardinality source can be used to explain why provider/demo tenant fan-out is noisy or should be suppressed in normal tenant-to-event traversals.
blocked_assertions: Do not turn high-cardinality provider/demo tenant fan-out into a positive access-path cluster.
Do not infer tenant ownership, compromise, actor control, direct user intent, operational effect, current access, or final assessment from high-cardinality fan-out.
A synthetic tenant-to-auth-event edge is not tenant ownership, compromise, actor control, direct user intent, operational effect, maliciousness, or final assessment.
Delegated, shared-service, provider, demo, automation, and health-check contexts require corroboration and suppression review before downstream systems treat them as meaningful access-path evidence.
Stale or historical auth-event metadata is not current access or active session context.
High-cardinality provider/demo tenant fan-out is suppression and rarity evidence, not a positive access-path cluster.
Validated lifecycle state is not a runtime confidence score, an attribution claim, or a live telemetry claim.
